🎬 Eleanor the Great (2025)

Eleanor the Great follows Eleanor Morgenstein, a spirited ninety-four-year-old woman who moves from Florida to New York City after the death of her closest friend, Bessie. Struggling with loneliness and the challenges of starting over at an advanced age, Eleanor unexpectedly joins a group of Holocaust survivors, where she shares a deeply personal story that actually belonged to her late friend. Her decision leads to an unlikely friendship with Nina, a young journalism student who becomes fascinated by Eleanor’s experiences. As their relationship grows stronger, Eleanor finds herself caught between the comfort of her newfound connections and the consequences of her deception. Forced to confront the truth, she begins to understand the importance of honesty, forgiveness, and preserving the memories of those we love. Starring June Squibb, Erin Kellyman, and Chiwetel Ejiofor, the film delivers heartfelt performances and emotional storytelling about grief, friendship, aging, identity, loneliness, and the universal desire to feel understood.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Comedy

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 38m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Scarlett Johansson

✍️ Writer: Tory Kamen

🎬 Production: Sony Pictures Classics

🏆 Recognition: Premiered at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival, marking Scarlett Johansson’s feature directorial debut.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Eleanor the Great is a 2025 American comedy-drama film directed by Scarlett Johansson, in her feature film directorial debut, and written by Tory Kamen. The film stars June Squibb supported by Erin Kellyman, Jessica Hecht, Rita Zohar, and Chiwetel Ejiofor. Its plot follows Eleanor Morgenstein, a 94-year-old woman, who strikes up an unlikely friendship with a 19-year-old student in New York City. It covers such themes as aging, Jewish identity, grief, and friendship. Eleanor the Great had its world premiere at the Un Certain Regard section of the Cannes Film Festival on May 20, 2025, and was released in the United States on September 26, 2025 by Sony Pictures Classics and TriStar Pictures.
